proposal.hypothesis: For long valid inputs, classifying ASCII ranges and applying arithmetic offsets across 32 input bytes should reduce scalar table lookups; vector dword shifts and a byte shuffle then pack 32 sextets into 24 bytes. Scalar decoding remains responsible for tails and padding. Any speedup remains unmeasured.

retained: Added AVX2 byte-range masks for A-Z, a-z, 0-9, '+' and '/', with arithmetic offsets to generate sextet values.
Packed four sextets per dword using vector shifts and OR operations, then used a lane-local byte shuffle to form output bytes.
Used full-width unaligned loads only when 32 input bytes remain; copied exactly 24 decoded bytes per block.
Left final padding and tails to the scalar decoder; fall back to scalar decoding of the full input if a vector block contains an invalid character.
Guarded AVX2 with a per-function target attribute and runtime CPU feature detection; retained the scalar path otherwise.

proposal.hypothesis: If per-character table lookups and serial bit assembly limit large valid inputs, decoding whole 32-character blocks with AVX2 range masks and arithmetic offsets, then vector bit packing, may improve throughput. Short inputs and tails may see no benefit; those and unsupported CPUs retain the scalar path.

retained: Classify each 32-byte input block with AVX2 range comparisons for uppercase, lowercase, digits, plus, and slash, then map sextets with arithmetic offsets and scalar-fallback on invalid blocks.
Pack the 32 sextets into 24 output bytes using AVX2 dword shifts, masks, and a byte shuffle; use an unaligned 32-byte load and exact-length memcpy stores.
Vectorize only a complete 32-character prefix after excluding terminal padding; decode any remaining characters, including padding and short tails, through the scalar decoder.
Keep AVX2 code in a GCC/Clang target("avx2") helper with runtime CPU feature dispatch; preserve scalar fallback and do not change build flags or add threads.
